mainTopic: Sources for the cases only the court of seventy-one may judge: a tribe, a נביא השקר, a כהן גדול, and a voluntary war
overview: The משנה lists cases that only the court of seventy-one may judge, and this amud looks for the reason behind several of them. First it asks what 'a tribe' means. רב מתנה's answer is a sinning נשיא, who is a 'great person'. A reading about land disputes is rejected, and רבינא adds that it can mean a whole tribe led into עבודה זרה. Next, a נביא השקר is linked to the זקן ממרא through the shared word 'דבר', after a link through 'הזדה' is rejected. A כהן גדול goes to the seventy-one because 'הדבר הגדול' means the matters of a great person, a reading that two ברייתות argue about. רבי אלעזר then asks about the כהן גדול's ox, and אביי infers that the כהן גדול's money cases go to an ordinary court. Finally, the גמרא looks for the source that a voluntary war needs the סנהדרין. It turns from a פסוק about יהושע to a story about דוד, and רב יוסף's request for the פסוק behind that story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The 'tribe' means a tribal leader who sinned
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה explains that the משנה's 'tribe' really means the נשיא of a tribe who sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with the leader of a tribe who sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving an answer to what the משנה means by 'judging a tribe'. It says the משנה is talking about the head of a tribe, not the whole tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'tribe' is read as 'the person who stands for the tribe', the נשיא. So the court of seventy-one is needed because of who is on trial. It is not about how many people are on trial.

keyTerms.meaning: The head or prince of a tribe

phrases.english: We are dealing with the leader of a tribe who sinned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of what 'tribe' in the משנה means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of 'tribe' case needs seventy-one judges?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נשיא of a tribe who committed a capital sin.

steps.title: Support from the verse about a 'great matter'
steps.stepSummary: Support from רב אדא בר אהבה: 'every great matter' means the cases of a great person, and a נשיא is a great person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רב אדא בר אהבה say: 'Every great matter they shall bring to you' means the matters of a great person? This נשיא is also a great person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב מתנה's answer with a known teaching. That teaching says important people are judged by the highest court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was told to judge the 'great matter' himself. רב אדא reads this as 'the matter of a great person'. משה stands for the great court of seventy-one, and a tribal נשיא is a 'great person', so his trial goes to that court.

keyTerms.meaning: The matters of a great person
Didn't (so-and-so) say?, a way of bringing support

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Didn't Rav Adda bar Ahava say:
"Every great matter they shall bring to you"
phrases.notes: שמות 18:22

phrases.english: meaning, the matters of a great person?
This one too is a great person.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that an important leader on trial for his life is judged by the highest court.
steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רב מתנה's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That a tribal נשיא is judged by seventy-one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אדא בר אהבה's reading of שמות 18:22: 'great matter' = matters of a great person.

steps.title: Another answer: tribes fighting over land
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר says the משנה is about tribes fighting over land, which needs seventy-one, just like the first division of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: it means when tribes come with a dispute over inheritance land, and it is like the beginning of ארץ ישראל. Just as at the beginning there were seventy-one, so too here there are seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives another meaning of 'tribe' in the משנה. Here it is a court case between tribes about land, not a criminal trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The land was first divided by seventy-one leaders. So a later fight about those borders should be decided by a body of the same size. This is an argument from comparison: the fix should match the original.

keyTerms.meaning: The first division of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
It is where they come over matters of inheritance,
phrases.notes: He means two tribes arguing over where the border between their lands lies.

phrases.english: and it is like the beginning of Eretz Yisrael.
Just as the beginning was with seventy-one,
so too here, seventy-one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same משנה instead of רב מתנה's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of 'tribe' case needs seventy-one judges?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A land dispute between tribes, modeled on the original division of the land.

steps.title: Then we would need lots, אורים ותומים and all Israel too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the comparison: the first division also used lots, the אורים ותומים and all of Israel, and nobody requires those for a border case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so: just as the beginning used lots, the אורים ותומים and all of Israel, so too here should we need lots, the אורים ותומים and all of Israel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's comparison. If we copy the first division, we would have to copy all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first division did not use only seventy-one elders. It also used a lottery, the כהן גדול's אורים ותומים, and the whole nation was there. No one requires those for a later border fight, so the comparison can't be used to require seventy-one either.

keyTerms.meaning: A lottery box, used to draw lots
The holy oracle in the כהן גדול's breastplate

phrases.english: If so, just as the beginning was with lots,
the Urim VeTummim, and all of Israel,
so too here, lots,
the Urim VeTummim, and all of Israel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison used in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא/רבי אלעזר's comparison of a border dispute to the first division of the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison proves too much. It would also require lots, the אורים ותומים and all Israel, which are clearly not required.

steps.title: Back to רב מתנה
steps.stepSummary: Since the land answer fails, the גמרא concludes the best answer is רב מתנה's: a sinning נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that it is like רב מתנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops עולא's answer. It goes back to the first answer, that the משנה means a tribal leader who sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחוורתא means 'it is clear'. It shows the גמרא is choosing the earlier answer because the other one fell apart. The proof from 'great matter' still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear / the clear answer is

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: it is as Rav Mattana said.

steps.whatToRemember: The land-dispute reading is rejected. The 'tribe' of the משנה means a sinning נשיא, judged by seventy-one because he is a 'great person'.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in step 4, returns to the answer of steps 1–2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב מתנה's explanation, a sinning tribal נשיא, is the accepted one.

steps.title: רבינא: really a tribe led into idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the משנה really means a whole tribe led into idol worship. Even though each is executed like an individual, they are still tried by the court of the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Actually it is a tribe that was led astray. And what bothered you, 'Do we judge it with the law of a group?' Yes. Even though we execute them as individuals, we judge them in the court of the group.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a new answer. He keeps the simple meaning of 'tribe', a whole tribe that served עבודה זרה, and answers the earlier difficulty with that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier difficulty was this: such a tribe is punished like individuals, by stoning and without losing their property, unlike an עיר הנדחת. So why would they need the big court? רבינא splits the two. The punishment follows the rules for individuals, but the trial still takes place in the court of seventy-one, the court for the many.

keyTerms.meaning: A tribe that was led astray into idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up how they are punished with where they are tried. They are executed like individuals, but the trial is still in the court of seventy-one.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, it is a tribe that was led astray,
and as for what was difficult for you:
Do we judge it with the law of a group?

phrases.aramaic: אִין, אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָטְלִינַן בְּיָחִיד,
phrases.english: Yes. Even though we execute them as individuals,
we judge them in the court of the many.

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא keeps 'tribe' as a whole tribe that sinned. Its members are punished as individuals but tried by the court of seventy-one.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the size of the court and the type of punishment are two separate questions.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different way to read the משנה, going back to the simple meaning that was challenged before רב מתנה's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting two rules: the type of court versus the type of punishment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a subverted tribe is executed as individuals, it should not need the court for the many.
steps.terutzMaskana: Punishment follows the individual rule, but the trial is still in the court of seventy-one.

steps.title: Proof that a whole tribe goes to the big court
steps.stepSummary: רבינא backs up his answer with a teaching of רבי אושעיא: only individuals are taken out 'to your gates', not a whole city. The same applies to a whole tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי חמא ברבי יוסי say in the name of רבי אושעיא: 'And you shall take out that man or that woman.' A man or a woman you take out to your gates, but you do not take out a whole city to your gates. Here too: a man or a woman you take out to your gates, but you do not take out a whole tribe to your gates.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא is proving his answer from step 6. A whole tribe that worshipped idols is judged by the seventy-one, even though each person is executed like an individual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to bring 'that man or that woman' to 'your gates', meaning the local court. רבי אושעיא learns from this that a whole city does not go to that local court. רבינא says a whole tribe is the same: a large group is never judged 'at your gates', so it must go to the big court of seventy-one.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't he say? This brings a known teaching as support.
To your gates, meaning the local court that sat at the city gate
Here too. It applies the same rule to a new case.

steps.whatToRemember: Individuals are judged 'at your gates', in the local court. A whole city or a whole tribe goes to the court of seventy-one.
steps.confusionAlert: The tribe members are still killed the way individual idol worshippers are killed. The only thing that changes here is which court judges them.

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Doesn't Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Yosei say
that Rabbi Oshaya said:
"And you shall take out that man
or that woman, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:5

phrases.english: A man or a woman you take out to your gates,
phrases.notes: "Your gates" means the local court that sat at the city gate.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מוֹצִיא כָּל הָעִיר כּוּלָּהּ לִשְׁעָרֶיךָ.
phrases.english: but you do not take out an entire city to your gates.
Here too:
A man or a woman you take out to your gates,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מוֹצִיא כׇּל הַשֵּׁבֶט כּוּלּוֹ לִשְׁעָרֶיךָ.
phrases.english: but you do not take out the entire tribe to your gates.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבינא's claim in step 6 that a whole tribe is tried by the court of seventy-one.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's reading that the משנה's 'tribe' case is a whole tribe that worshipped idols, judged by seventy-one
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אושעיא's reading of דברים 17:5: individuals go 'to your gates', but a whole city does not

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule for a false prophet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next case in the משנה, the נביא השקר, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor a false prophet', except by the court of seventy-one. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next case in the משנה. It asks for the source, which sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said only the court of seventy-one can judge a נביא השקר. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things known? It asks for a source.

phrases.english: Nor a false prophet.
From where are these words derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tribe topic and opens a new question about the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a נביא השקר is judged only by the court of seventy-one

steps.title: Learning from the word 'presumptuousness'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns the rule through a גזירה שוה: the word 'הזדה' appears for both the false prophet and the זקן ממרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: We learn 'presumptuousness' here from 'presumptuousness' said about the rebellious elder. Just as there it is with seventy-one, so too here it is with seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the question. He links the false prophet to the זקן ממרא because the same word appears in both sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word 'הזדה', acting presumptuously. The זקן ממרא's case involves the court of seventy-one, so the shared word carries that over to the false prophet.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from. This introduces a link between two פסוקים.
Acting presumptuously, on purpose against authority
A rebellious elder: a sage who rules against the סנהדרין הגדולה
Just as there, so too here

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
It is learned from "presumptuousness" and "presumptuousness"
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are דברים 18:20 (the false prophet) and דברים 17:12 (the rebellious elder).

phrases.english: from the rebellious elder.
Just as there it is with seventy-one,
so too here it is with seventy-one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'הזדה' links the false prophet to the זקן ממרא, whose case involves seventy-one

steps.title: That word is about the death penalty, which needs only twenty-three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the link: 'הזדה' by the זקן ממרא appears in the פסוק about his death, and a death sentence only needs a court of twenty-three.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where 'presumptuousness' is written, it is written about killing him, and killing is done by a court of twenty-three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's source. The word he used is tied to the wrong part of the זקן ממרא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הזדה' sits in the פסוק that sentences the זקן ממרא to death. A death sentence is handled by twenty-three judges, so this word can only teach twenty-three, not seventy-one.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! This opens a challenge.
Twenty-three, the size of a court that can rule on capital cases

phrases.english: But when "presumptuousness" is written,
it is written about the death penalty,
and the death penalty is given by twenty-three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's גזירה שוה from 'הזדה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The shared word is in the death-penalty פסוק, and a death sentence needs only twenty-three, so the link proves twenty-three, not seventy-one.

steps.title: Learning from the word 'word' instead
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a new source: the word 'דבר' links the false prophet to the זקן ממרא's actual rebellion against the court of seventy-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, ריש לקיש said: He learns 'word' from 'word' used about the elder's rebellion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first source and brings ריש לקיש's better one. It uses a word tied to the rebellion itself, not to the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זקן ממרא rebels against 'the word that they will tell you', and that ruling comes from the court of seventy-one. The false prophet 'speaks a word' presumptuously. Since 'דבר' is tied to the seventy-one, the link teaches that the false prophet is judged by seventy-one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier answer and gives a new one.
He learns, through a link between words
Rebellion, the elder's ruling against the סנהדרין הגדולה

steps.whatToRemember: A false prophet is judged by seventy-one because of the word 'דבר', which ties him to the זקן ממרא's rebellion against the סנהדרין הגדולה. The link through 'הזדה' was rejected because it only connects to the death penalty.

phrases.english: Rather, Reish Lakish said:
He learns "word" from "word"
from his rebellion.
phrases.notes: For the elder it is דברים 17:10, "according to the word they tell you"; for the prophet it is דברים 18:20, "speak a word".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 10 with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The link could come from 'הזדה', but that word only connects to the death penalty, which needs twenty-three.
steps.terutzMaskana: The link comes from 'דבר', which connects to the rebellion against the court of seventy-one.

steps.title: Why not use the 'הזדה' link the other way for the זקן ממרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: let the זקן ממרא learn from the נביא השקר through 'הזדה' that he too is judged by seventy-one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let us go back to the זקן ממרא and learn 'הזדה' and 'הזדה' from the false prophet?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. It asks why we don't flip the 'הזדה' link around. The false prophet is judged by seventy-one, so the זקן ממרא should be judged by seventy-one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 the 'הזדה' link was rejected as a source for the false prophet, because a זקן ממרא is put to death by a court of twenty-three. Now that 'דבר' has shown the false prophet needs seventy-one, the גמרא asks why 'הזדה' should not carry that rule back to the זקן ממרא's death sentence.

keyTerms.meaning: let it go back / turn around
acting with bold defiance (the shared word)

phrases.english: And let the rebellious elder go back
phrases.notes: Meaning: turn the comparison around, so the זקן ממרא is now the one learning.

phrases.english: and learn 'presumptuousness' 'presumptuousness' from the false prophet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on ריש לקיש's 'דבר' answer and asks why the rejected 'הזדה' link can't still work in reverse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The court size of the זקן ממרא, which is assumed to be twenty-three
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the words 'הזדה' and 'הזדה' are linked, the link should pass the false prophet's court of seventy-one over to the זקן ממרא.

steps.title: This תנא learns only the 'דבר' link
steps.stepSummary: The תנא uses the 'דבר' link but does not use the 'הזדה' link at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'דבר' and 'דבר'; he does not learn 'הזדה' and 'הזדה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this תנא simply does not accept the 'הזדה' link. Since there is no link, nothing can be passed in either direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is not something anyone can invent. A תנא uses only the links he has received from his teachers. This תנא has 'דבר' but not 'הזדה', so the זקן ממרא stays with a court of twenty-three.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not learn / did not receive
a teaching learned from the same word in two places

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the 'הזדה' link is weaker logically. It is saying this תנא doesn't use that link at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The false prophet is judged by seventy-one through 'דבר'. The זקן ממרא's death sentence stays with twenty-three, because this תנא does not use 'הזדה'.

phrases.english: 'Word' 'word' he learns,
'presumptuousness' 'presumptuousness' he does not learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by denying that the 'הזדה' link exists for this תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise: the link being used is not accepted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'הזדה' link could pass seventy-one over to the זקן ממרא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'דבר' is a valid link for this תנא, so 'הזדה' teaches nothing.

steps.title: Source for judging the כהן גדול only by seventy-one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, the כהן גדול, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not the כהן גדול' except by the court of seventy-one. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case from the משנה. It asks where we learn that only the great court of seventy-one can judge a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic. Before this, the cases were a tribe and a false prophet. Now the case is a person of very high rank, and the גמרא wants a פסוק to back up the rule.

phrases.english: And not the High Priest.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the false-prophet discussion and turns to the next case in the משנה, just as Step 8 did.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a כהן גדול is judged only by the court of seventy-one.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: 'the great matter' means matters of a great person
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה reads 'כל הדבר הגדול יביאו אליך' as cases about a great person, meaning the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: The פסוק says 'Every great matter they shall bring to you.' This means the matters of a great person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה gives the source. The פסוק tells משה that the 'great matter' should be brought to him, and he reads this as the cases of a great person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה stands in place of the great court of seventy-one. רב אדא reads 'הדבר הגדול' not as 'a big case' but as 'the case of the great one', the כהן גדול. So the כהן גדול's case goes to the court of seventy-one.

keyTerms.meaning: the matters of a great person

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
For the verse says:
'Every great matter they shall bring to you,'
phrases.notes: שמות 18:22

phrases.english: the matters of a great one.
phrases.notes: The 'great one' here is the כהן גדול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'הדבר הגדול' in שמות 18:22 means the cases of a great person, the כהן גדול, which go to משה or the great court.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads 'great matter' as 'difficult matter'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'דבר גדול' means a difficult case. It proves this from the later פסוק, 'את הדבר הקשה יביאון אל משה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: 'A great matter' means a difficult matter. Do you say it means a difficult matter, or perhaps it means the matters of a great person? When it says 'The difficult matter they would bring to משה,' a difficult matter is stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא with a ברייתא. That ברייתא says 'דבר גדול' means a hard case, not a great person's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares two פסוקים. The first is יתרו's advice, 'the great matter'. The second is what משה actually did, 'the difficult matter'. Since משה carried out the advice, 'great' must mean 'difficult', which leaves no room for רב אדא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'A great matter' means a difficult matter.
Do you say it means a difficult matter,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל גָּדוֹל?
phrases.english: or is it only the matters of a great one?
When it says
'The difficult matter they would bring to Moshe,'
phrases.notes: שמות 18:26. This is what משה actually did after יתרו's advice.

phrases.english: a difficult matter is stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אדא's reading of the פסוק from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's reading of 'דבר גדול' as 'the matters of a great one'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later פסוק shows that the 'great matter' is a 'difficult matter', so the phrase cannot be the source for the כהן גדול.

steps.title: רב אדא follows a different ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא agrees with another תנא. That תנא argues that since 'הדבר הקשה' already covers hard cases, 'דבר גדול' must mean a great person's cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like this תנא, as it was taught: 'A great matter' means the matters of a great person. Do you say that, or perhaps it means a difficult matter? When it says 'the difficult matter,' a difficult matter is already stated. So how do I explain 'a great matter'? It means the matters of a great person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב אדא is not alone. A different ברייתא reads the פסוק exactly his way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות look at the same two פסוקים but draw opposite conclusions. The first says the second פסוק explains the first: 'great' means 'difficult'. The second says that since 'difficult' already has its own words, 'great' must be teaching something extra, the cases of a great person.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
how do I give meaning to (this phrase)?

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות use the very same פסוק, 'הדבר הקשה'. One uses it to explain 'great'. The other uses it to say 'great' must mean something different.
steps.whatToRemember: The source that a כהן גדול is judged by seventy-one is 'דבר גדול', read as the matters of a great person. This follows the second ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern in the גמרא: an אמורא challenged by one ברייתא is defended by showing he follows another תנא.

phrases.english: He states it in accordance with this tanna,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: as it is taught:
'A great matter' means the matters of a great one.
Do you say it means the matters of a great one,
or is it only a difficult matter?
When it says 'the difficult matter,'
a difficult matter is already stated.
So how do I explain 'a great matter'?
The matters of a great one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 by pointing to a ברייתא that agrees with רב אדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The answer is that this is a disagreement between תנאים, and רב אדא follows the other ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first ברייתא shows that 'דבר גדול' only means a difficult case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another תנא holds that 'הדבר הקשה' already covers difficult cases, so 'דבר גדול' means the matters of a great person, and רב אדא follows him.

steps.title: Why would the first תנא need two פסוקים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first תנא, who reads both 'דבר גדול' and 'דבר קשה' as hard cases. If they mean the same thing, why does the תורה write two פסוקים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא: why do I need two verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the first תנא, who says both פסוקים mean difficult cases. It asks why the תורה would say the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the תורה does not repeat itself for no reason. If 'דבר גדול' and 'דבר קשה' both mean a hard case, one פסוק looks extra. So this תנא must explain what the second פסוק adds.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the משנה or ברייתא period
Why do I need it? (a question asking what something adds)

phrases.english: And this תנא,
phrases.notes: He means the first ברייתא from step 16, which says 'דבר גדול' means a hard case.

phrases.english: why do I need two verses?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי תַּנָּא, תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After seeing how the second תנא reads the פסוקים, the גמרא now challenges the first תנא's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's reading that both 'דבר גדול' and 'דבר קשה' refer to difficult cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both פסוקים teach the same thing, one of them is extra, and the תורה does not write extra words.

steps.title: One פסוק is the instruction and the other is the doing
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא answers that the two פסוקים do not repeat each other. One gives the instruction, and the other reports that it was actually carried out.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is for the command in general, and one is for the doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the first תנא. The first פסוק is the instruction, and the second tells us it was actually done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים do talk about hard cases going to משה. But they are not extra, because one records the plan and the other records the plan being carried out. So the first תנא does not need two separate laws.

keyTerms.meaning: The doing; actually carrying it out

phrases.english: One is for the command in general,
phrases.notes: This is יתרו's advice to משה (שמות 18:22). The other פסוק (שמות 18:26) tells us they really did it.

phrases.english: and one is for the doing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns a different purpose to each פסוק without creating a new law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two פסוקים with the same meaning look like a needless repetition.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק is the instruction and the other reports how it was carried out, so neither is extra.

steps.title: Why doesn't the other תנא accept this answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the second תנא does not explain the two פסוקים the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next move. It asks why the second תנא will not accept the 'instruction and doing' explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 gave a good reason for having two פסוקים. So the גמרא now asks what forces the second תנא to read 'דבר גדול' as a new law about a great person.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (asking how the other opinion handles the point)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: He means the second תנא from step 17, who reads 'דבר גדול' as a great person's cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 19 into a question on the second תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the second תנא rejects the 'instruction and doing' explanation of the two פסוקים.

steps.title: Different words mean two different laws
steps.stepSummary: The second תנא says that if both פסוקים meant the same thing, the תורה would have used the same word twice. Since it wrote 'גדול' in one and 'קשה' in the other, we learn two laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it write either 'great' and 'great', or 'difficult' and 'difficult'. Why 'great' and why 'difficult'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second תנא's view. The change of wording between the two פסוקים shows that each one teaches something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second תנא answers that if one פסוק were only the instruction and the other only the doing, the same word should appear in both. Because the תורה switched from 'גדול' to 'קשה', we learn both rules: hard cases go up, and so do the cases of a great person, the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it write; it should have written

steps.whatToRemember: The first תנא: both פסוקים mean hard cases, one as the instruction and one as the doing. The second תנא: the change in wording teaches two laws, hard cases and a כהן גדול's cases.

phrases.english: If so,
let it write either 'great' and 'great',
or 'difficult' and 'difficult'.
Why 'great' and why 'difficult'?
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב אוֹ גָּדוֹל גָּדוֹל, אוֹ קָשֶׁה קָשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The change in wording between the two פסוקים shows they teach two separate laws: difficult cases and a great person's cases.

steps.title: How many judges try the כהן גדול's ox?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks how many judges are needed when the ox of a כהן גדול kills a person. Do we treat it like a trial that could put the כהן גדול himself to death, or like any owner?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: the ox of a כהן גדול, with how many judges is it judged? Do we compare it to the death of its own owner, or do we compare it to the death of owners in general?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a question about an ox that killed someone when its owner is a כהן גדול. Should it be judged by 71 like the כהן גדול himself, or by the usual 23?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides are clear. A trial that could kill the כהן גדול needs 71 judges, and a trial for an ox normally needs 23. רבי אלעזר asks whether the ox follows its own special owner or follows the normal rule for any owner.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question that needs an answer)

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר asked:
The ox of a כהן גדול, with how many judges?
phrases.notes: He means an ox that killed a person, which must be put on trial.

phrases.english: Do we compare it to the death of its own owner,
or perhaps to the death of owners in general
do we compare it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שׁוֹרוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, בְּכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that a כהן גדול's cases go to the 71 and asks how far that rule reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the trial of a כהן גדול's ox follows the trial of its owner (71 judges) or the trial of a regular owner (23 judges).

steps.title: אביי: his money cases are clearly a regular court
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רבי אלעזר asked only about the ox. That shows he held it was obvious that the כהן גדול's other money cases go to an ordinary court.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: since he asked about his ox, we can infer that his money was obvious to him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a lesson from the way רבי אלעזר asked his question. Because he asked only about the ox, he must have been sure about the כהן גדול's ordinary money matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox case has a special reason to compare it to the owner: the ox's trial is about death, like the owner's. Plain money cases have no such reason, so רבי אלעזר did not even ask about them. They are judged by a regular court.

phrases.english: אביי said:
Since he asked about his ox,
we can infer that his money was obvious to him.
phrases.notes: Obvious in which direction? That the כהן גדול's money cases go to an ordinary court, not to the 71.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִדְּקָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ שׁוֹרוֹ, מִכְלָל דְּמָמוֹנוֹ פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side lesson from how רבי אלעזר framed his question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money cases of a כהן גדול are judged by an ordinary court, not the 71.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי needed to say this, since it seems obvious that money cases do not need 71 judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's inference as something everyone already knows. This one-word challenge sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that needs no proof should not need a teaching. So the גמרא asks what אביי's point adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for אביי's inference.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's inference that a כהן גדול's money cases go to an ordinary court.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money cases clearly do not need the 71, so stating it seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: Someone might have read 'כל הדבר הגדול' as every case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק says 'כל הדבר הגדול', and one might have thought this covers every kind of case of a great person, even money. אביי teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it is written 'every great matter', all matters of a great person go there. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי's point was needed. The word 'כל' (every) could have made us think all of the כהן גדול's cases go to the 71.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'כל' made it seem that even money cases are included. אביי's inference shows that this is not so. Only the serious cases, like a death penalty trial, go to the 71.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introducing a mistaken idea)

phrases.english: You might have said:
since it is written 'every great matter',
phrases.notes: שמות 18:22

phrases.english: all matters of a great person go there,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְכָתַב כׇּל הַדָּבָר הַגָּדֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable mistaken idea to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק says 'כל', every case of a כהן גדול, even money, would go to the 71.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן גדול's money cases go to an ordinary court; 'כל' does not include them.

steps.title: Source that a voluntary war needs the 71
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, that the people are taken out to a voluntary war only by the 71-judge court, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not take out (to war), etc. From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, going out to a voluntary war. It asks where we learn that this needs the 71-judge court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern the גמרא used for the כהן גדול case: quote the משנה, then ask for the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not take out (the people to war)
A voluntary war, one the תורה does not command

phrases.english: They do not take out, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה's full line: a king takes the people out to a voluntary war only by the court of 71.

phrases.english: From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a voluntary war requires the court of 71.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: 'He shall stand before אלעזר הכהן'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings the פסוק about יהושע standing before אלעזר הכהן as the source for needing the 71-judge court to go to war.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: because the verse says, 'And he shall stand before אלעזר הכהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question with a פסוק about how יהושע, the leader, must stand before אלעזר הכהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes on to say that by his word they go out and come in, which means going out to war. So the leader may not go to war on his own; he needs approval. Here רבי אבהו only quotes the פסוק, and the next lines will explain how it points to the 71-judge court.

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said:
because the verse says
'And he shall stand before אלעזר הכהן.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:21, said about יהושע.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: דְּאָמַר קְרָא וְלִפְנֵי אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן יַעֲמֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ולפני אלעזר הכהן יעמד' shows that the leader goes out to war only by the word of a higher authority.

steps.title: Each part of the פסוק matched to a leader
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains the end of the פסוק. 'He' is the king, 'all the children of Israel with him' is the כהן משוח מלחמה, and 'all the congregation' is the סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He' means the king. 'And all the children of Israel with him' means the priest anointed for war. 'And all the congregation' means the סנהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו shows how the פסוק from the last step proves that a war needs the סנהדרין. He matches each phrase in the פסוק to a different leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'congregation' (עדה) is read as the סנהדרין. Since the פסוק puts the סנהדרין right next to the king in the decision to go out and come in, the king seems to need the סנהדרין to go to war.

keyTerms.meaning: King. Here it covers יהושע and any leader who takes the nation to war.
The כהן who is anointed to speak to the army before a war
Congregation. Here it is read as the סנהדרין.

phrases.english: 'He' – this is the king,
phrases.notes: This is the end of the פסוק about יהושע and אלעזר הכהן, במדבר 27:21.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכׇל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִתּוֹ״ – זֶה מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה,
phrases.english: 'And all the children of Israel with him' – this is the priest anointed for war,
'And all the congregation' – this is the Sanhedrin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי אבהו's proof from the פסוק he brought in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: A voluntary war needs the 71-judge court.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 27:21, where 'all the congregation' is read as the סנהדרין.

steps.title: Maybe the סנהדרין is mentioned only for asking the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. Maybe the פסוק mentions the סנהדרין only to teach that it may ask questions of the אורים ותומים, not that it must approve a war.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the תורה is telling the סנהדרין that it may ask questions of the אורים ותומים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבהו's proof. It suggests a different reason the פסוק mentions the סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק is talking about asking questions through the אורים ותומים in front of אלעזר הכהן. So listing the סנהדרין there may only mean the סנהדרין is allowed to ask such questions. If so, the פסוק says nothing about the סנהדרין having to agree before a king goes to war.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe (opens another way to read the source)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
The holy names in the כהן גדול's breastplate, used to get answers from heaven

phrases.english: But perhaps it is to the Sanhedrin
that the Merciful One is saying to them,
that they may ask of the Urim VeTummim?
phrases.notes: In other words, the סנהדרין may ask questions just like the king can, but that doesn't mean the king needs its permission for war.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא לְסַנְהֶדְרֵי הוּא דְּקָאָמַר לְהוּ רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 28 reads the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's proof that 'all the congregation' (the סנהדרין) must approve a war.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק talks about the אורים ותומים, so mentioning the סנהדרין may only give it the right to ask questions. It does not have to mean the סנהדרין must give permission.

steps.title: A new source: the lyre over דוד's bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the proof from the פסוק and starts a story from רבי שמעון חסידא. A lyre over דוד's bed played by itself at midnight, דוד learned תורה until dawn, and then the חכמים came to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is like what רב אחא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא. A lyre hung above דוד's bed. At midnight the north wind blew on it and it played by itself. דוד would get up right away and learn תורה until dawn. When dawn came, the חכמי ישראל came in to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and switches to a different source. This step only sets up the story; the proof comes later in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) tells us the proof from the פסוק is being set aside. The scene of the חכמים coming to the king each morning is what leads to the talk about going to war.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, the first light of morning

steps.confusionAlert: The lyre story is not itself the proof. The proof comes at the end of this story, when the king consults the court before going to war.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like that which
phrases.notes: The proof from the פסוק is being dropped. The real proof is at the end of this story, which goes on past the conversation in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Bizna says
that Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida says:
A lyre was hanging
above the bed of David.
Once midnight arrived,
the north wind would blow on it
and it would play by itself.
Immediately David would get up
and study Torah
until the dawn rose.
Once the dawn rose,
the Sages of Israel would come in to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29 by bringing a different source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: the proof from the פסוק is dropped and a story about דוד's practice is brought instead.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק about יהושע proves that the סנהדרין must approve a war.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is the story of דוד, which will show him consulting the court before war.

steps.title: The nation needs a living, so דוד sends them to battle
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell דוד the nation needs a living. He tells them to support each other. They answer that the nation cannot support itself from its own resources, so דוד tells them to go out with the troops.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Our master the king, your nation Israel needs a living. He said to them: Go and support one another. They said to him: A handful does not fill up a lion, and a pit is not filled from the rain falling into its own mouth. He said to them: Go and stretch out your hands with the troops.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on with a conversation between דוד and the חכמים about the nation's need for a living. It ends with דוד telling them to go out to war, which leads into the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד first suggests a solution from inside the nation, with people helping each other. The חכמים answer with two comparisons that show the nation's own resources are not enough. That is why going out to war comes up, and this kind of war, fought to gain a living, is a voluntary war.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit or cistern for water

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the kind of war under discussion. It is a war fought to expand the land and give people a living, not a war to defend against an attack.

phrases.english: They said to him: Our master the king,
your nation Israel needs a livelihood.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: לְכוּ וְהִתְפַּרְנְסוּ זֶה מִזֶּה.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go and support yourselves from one another.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין הַקּוֹמֶץ מַשְׂבִּיעַ אֶת הָאֲרִי,
phrases.english: They said to him: A handful does not satisfy the lion,
and a pit is not filled from its own mouth.
phrases.notes: The rain that falls straight into a pit's opening won't fill it. Water has to come in from outside, and the nation is the same.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לְכוּ פִּשְׁטוּ יְדֵיכֶם בִּגְדוּד.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go stretch out your hands with the troop.
phrases.notes: He means: go out to battle with the army.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֲדוֹנֵינוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ, עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל צְרִיכִין לְפַרְנָסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד answers the nation's economic need by sending the people out to a voluntary war.

steps.title: Before war: advice, סנהדרין approval, then the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: The story ends. Once war was decided, they first got advice from אחיתופל, then got approval from the סנהדרין, and then asked the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away they would get advice from אחיתופל, consult with the סנהדרין, and ask the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי שמעון חסידא's story. It lists the three things done before going to war, and one of them is going to the סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why the גמרא told the story. The פסוק proof in steps 27-28 was pushed off, because the סנהדרין might only have been there to ask the אורים ותומים. Here the סנהדרין has its own separate role, consulting on whether to go to war, apart from asking the אורים ותומים.

keyTerms.meaning: They consult with and get approval from

steps.confusionAlert: Don't merge the סנהדרין step with the אורים ותומים step. They are two separate actions. That is exactly what answers the challenge in step 29.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real source for the rule in the משנה that going to war needs the court of 71.

phrases.english: Immediately they would take advice from אחיתופל,
and consult with the סנהדרין,
and ask the אורים ותומים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in step 30. After דוד says 'go out with the troops' (step 31), it shows the steps taken before war.
steps.raayaObject: That going to war needs approval from the סנהדרין, separate from asking the אורים ותומים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי שמעון חסידא about דוד and the חכמים.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks which פסוק the story is based on
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks which פסוק teaches this order of advice, סנהדרין, and אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Which פסוק is this based on?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks for the פסוק behind the story. This line sets up his answer, which is quoted at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story alone is not enough. The גמרא wants to anchor each part (אחיתופל, the סנהדרין, the אורים ותומים) in a פסוק. So the answer should show each of the three named separately.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who asks for the source

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the פסוק that backs up the order of events in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק shows דוד's order of getting advice from אחיתופל, approval from the סנהדרין, and asking the אורים ותומים.
